meta.name: Synthetic sensor anomaly detection on AWS

data.label: Synthetic sensor devices
data.description: Existing synthetic event generator. Each event carries device_id, timestamp and value+unit. Outside provisioning scope.

data.label: Ingestion
data.description: Authenticates devices over MQTT and routes events via an IoT rule into Kinesis. Device certificates/policies need design.

data.label: Durable buffer
data.description: Durable, ordered buffer partitioned by device_id so events can be replayed. Retention period to be decided.

data.label: Validation & scoring
data.description: Consumes Kinesis batches; validates schema, device_id, timestamp and unit without altering them; sends invalid events to quarantine; calls the model; writes results idempotently keyed by device_id+timestamp; publishes alerts above threshold. Owns its role and logs.

data.label: Invalid event quarantine
data.description: Holds events that fail validation or processing, with the reason, for review and replay.

data.label: Anomaly model
data.description: Returns an anomaly score per event. Local tests use a scripted response; real accuracy needs a trained model and labelled evaluation.

data.label: Anomaly results
data.description: Stores device_id, timestamp, original value+unit, score, model version and decision.

data.label: Operator alert
data.description: Publishes anomaly alerts with device_id, timestamp and score. Subscription channel to be decided.

data.label: Operator
data.description: Person who receives and acts on anomaly alerts.

brief.application: Use AWS for this synthetic architecture qualification. Analyze synthetic sensor events for anomalous device behavior. Preserve device identity, timestamps and units. Include ingestion, durable buffering, validation, inference, results and an operator alert. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

lastAsked.question: How much history do you have for what you want to predict?
lastAsked.beginner: For example “three years of sales by store” or “failure records since 2020”.
lastAsked.why: It shapes the Predictive ML design.

requirements.statement: Every stored result and alert must keep the original device_id, event timestamp and value with its unit unchanged.
requirements.rationale: If identity, time or units are lost, operators can't trace or trust an anomaly.
requirements.basis: User: "Preserve device identity, timestamps and units."

requirements.statement: Events that fail validation are kept with a reason in a quarantine queue and are never scored or silently dropped.
requirements.rationale: Proposed: prevents bad data from causing false alarms while keeping it for replay.
requirements.basis: User requested validation and durable buffering.

requirements.statement: An operator is notified when an event's anomaly score crosses the agreed threshold; the threshold and false-alarm tolerance are still open.
requirements.rationale: Too many false alarms make operators ignore alerts; too few miss failures.

decisions.subject: design.end-to-end-aws-sensor-anomaly-detection-sketch
decisions.title: End-to-end AWS sensor anomaly detection sketch
decisions.context: Scope: ingestion (IoT Core), durable buffering (Kinesis Data Streams), validation and scoring (Lambda), inference (SageMaker endpoint), quarantine for invalid events (SQS), results (DynamoDB) and operator alert (SNS). Assumptions: synthetic devices are existing callers outside provisioning; region and account are not selected; model type and labels are open. None of these paths has native generator coverage yet, so each remains an engineering gap. This is not a deployment.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.
